汗.meaning: In a heatwave, an old wooden <part>drying rack</part> holds up fourteen wet towels, three duvets and a cat. It creaks, it groans, and <part>water drops</part> bead all over its poles. By evening the laundry is dry, but the rack isn't: it's dripping with <kanji>sweat</kanji>.
汗.on: The family pins a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to it for being so brave.
汗.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' it creaks, as the sun <sound>se</sound>ts at last.

賀.meaning: Every time a pearl diver comes up with a <part>shellfish</part>, her crew <part>add</part> it to the pile and cheer louder. By the hundredth they're dancing, singing and hugging the seagulls, and the last shell holds a pearl the size of a plum. The whole boat is pure <kanji>joy</kanji>.
賀.on: That night they party on deck with prawns and <sound>ga</sound>rlic bread.

渉.meaning: A postman's van breaks down at a river, so he takes off his boots and goes for a <part>walk</part> straight through the cold <part>water drops</part>, mailbag on his head and fish nibbling his toes. Every letter arrives on time. No bridge needed: he knows where to <kanji>ford</kanji> it.
渉.on: On the far bank the villagers clap as if it's a <sound>show</sound>.
渉.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' he yells as a fish nips him, and drops his <sound>ta</sound>co in the river.

拭.meaning: At a ship's naming <part>ceremony</part>, the mayor swings the bottle, misses the hull and soaks the admiral. Then the crew hauls up the muddy <part>anchor</part> and it drips all over the band. A cabin boy runs along the deck with one tiny towel. He has a lot to <kanji>wipe</kanji>.
拭.on: When he dries the band's microphone, he gets a little <sound>shock</sound>.
拭.kun: Afterwards he hides in a <sound>noo</sound>k below deck with a <sound>goo</sound>die bag of sweets.

搬.meaning: A tired <part>carrier</part> who rows goods across the harbour is sick of lifting crates. She ties her <part>anchor</part> rope round a loop of wooden rollers, and now every crate slides up from her boat to the warehouse on its own. She just sits and waves at them. She has invented the <kanji>conveyor</kanji>.
搬.on: The first crate up is full of jars of <sound>hon</sound>ey, and a bee rides along on top.

晶.meaning: A miner digs up a stone with three tiny <part>sun</part> shapes trapped inside. When she holds it to the window, each one throws rainbows round her hut, and her dog chases them for hours. Even at night it glows. She has never seen anything <kanji>sparkle</kanji> like that.
晶.on: She takes it on tour as the star of a travelling <sound>show</sound>.

秒.meaning: A chef drops a <part>few</part> kernels of <part>grain</part> into a sizzling pan and turns to fetch the salt. Pop, pop, pop! Before she turns back, every one has burst and flown out of the window. Popcorn waits for nobody: it's done in one <kanji>second</kanji>.
秒.on: Outside, a ba<sound>by</sound> bats each one away with his <sound>yo</sound>-yo.
